A NOTE BEFORE WE START

New to wayfinding.
Experienced in making.

I’m a graphic designer with experience in label design, print production and digital projects. I haven’t yet worked professionally in signage planning.

This is a self-initiated exercise showing how I approach an unfamiliar brief: research, organise, prototype and identify what needs expert review.

02 / DESIGN REASONING

Information where
the decision happens.

A first-time visitor is the starting point. The system introduces the building at arrival, confirms direction at a junction and identifies the room at the end.

01

Orient at the entrance

A directory establishes the floor and destination structure before the visitor starts moving.

02

Guide at the junction

Directional signs belong at decision points. A route to the first floor uses the lift in this concept.

03

Confirm at the door

Consistent room names and numbers connect the directory, directions and final room identification.

04 / THE PERSON BEHIND THE STUDY

I bring experience.
And room to learn.

My background includes label design and production work at Securikett and campaign work at GGK MullenLowe. Alongside that, I have taught myself to build and release digital projects, including an Android app on Google Play.

I bring that same resourcefulness here: breaking down a brief, learning the tools and turning the work into something that can be tested and discussed.

A note on language

My spoken English is stronger than my spoken German. I understand German well, but I’m still developing the fluency and confidence needed for professional discussions.

What this study does — and doesn’t — claim

This fictional concept demonstrates information design, linked documentation and a proposed visitor route. It is not client work, a surveyed building or a compliant installation package. Emergency signage, tactile guidance, accessible circulation, mounting heights, materials and applicable standards would require qualified review before implementation. No employer affiliation or approval is implied.
